title: FARL: Use Factor-Augmented Regularized Latent Regression for Large-Scale Assessment
text: FARL package implements factor-augmented regularized latent regression (FARLR) large-scale assessments. FARLR addresses high-dimensional, strongly dependent background variables decomposing variation common latent factors idiosyncratic components. common factors enter latent regression, sparse regularization selects parsimonious set relevant idiosyncratic covariates. multidimensional assessments, MFARLR extends structure several correlated latent traits. estimates regression coefficients full residual covariance jointly, avoiding separate pairwise covariance fits preserving dependence among dimensions plausible values generated group-level analyses. package supports: unidimensional FARLR estimation Farlr_mml(); unidimensional PCA-based DIRE estimation Dire_mml(); multidimensional FARLR-GVEM estimation MFARLR_mml(); multidimensional DIRE estimation MDIRE_mml(); plausible-value generation fitted models. development version can installed

title: FARL: Use Factor-Augmented Regularized Latent Regression for Large-Scale Assessment
text: Multidimensional large-scale assessments must model high-dimensional, correlated background variables dependence among latent traits. PCA-population model can discard low-variance covariate information remains predictive achievement, fitting latent-trait covariances separately can yield incoherent covariance estimate. MFARLR instead combines common factors sparsely selected covariates estimates dimensions jointly. multidimensional functions retain compact data interface. models receive X, Y, parTab; item slopes, intercepts, dimension assignments obtained parTab internally.

title: FARL: Use Factor-Augmented Regularized Latent Regression for Large-Scale Assessment
text: MFARLR uses three steps. First, factor analysis summarizes common variation standardized covariates. Second, FARLR_Debias screens covariates within latent dimension, retaining predictors selected least one dimension. Third, selected sparsity pattern held fixed GVEM jointly updates coefficient matrix, person-specific variational moments, full latent residual covariance. Gaussian variational posterior makes updates computationally feasible without multidimensional quadrature.

title: FARL: Use Factor-Augmented Regularized Latent Regression for Large-Scale Assessment
text: two PV outputs first restored original sim_m1 subject order. PV1 extracted separately every latent dimension. Correlation RMSE provide compact simulation check latent-distribution recovery; applied analysis, inference combine estimates across plausible values rather treating single draw observed score. following figure overlays two sets PVs every dimension. Solid lines method-specific regressions dashed line identity line. shared legend placed final panel avoid covering data. # Main Outputs
code: N <- nrow(sim_m1$X) D <- ncol(sim_m1$theta) subject_order <- as.character(seq_len(N))  order_PVs <- function(dat) {   row_order <- match(subject_order, as.character(dat$id))   if (anyNA(row_order)) {     stop("Some subjects are missing from the PV output.")   }   dat <- dat[row_order, , drop = FALSE]   rownames(dat) <- NULL   dat }  mfarlr_dat <- order_PVs(mfarlr_PVs$datPVs) dire_dat <- order_PVs(dire_PVs$data)  mfarlr_first_PV <- sapply(   seq_len(D),   function(dimension) {     mfarlr_dat[[paste0("_mfarlr_D", dimension, "_PV1")]]   } )  dire_first_PV <- sapply(   seq_len(D),   function(dimension) {     subtest <- dire_mmlcomp$subtest_names[dimension]     dire_dat[[paste0(subtest, "_dire1")]]   } )  dimension_names <- paste0("Dimension", seq_len(D)) colnames(mfarlr_first_PV) <- dimension_names colnames(dire_first_PV) <- dimension_names  multidimensional_comparison <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(seq_len(D), function(dimension) {     truth <- sim_m1$theta[, dimension]     mfarlr_error <- mfarlr_first_PV[, dimension] - truth     dire_error <- dire_first_PV[, dimension] - truth      data.frame(       dimension = dimension,       MFARLR_correlation = stats::cor(         truth,         mfarlr_first_PV[, dimension]       ),       DIRE_correlation = stats::cor(         truth,         dire_first_PV[, dimension]       ),       MFARLR_RMSE = sqrt(mean(mfarlr_error^2)),       DIRE_RMSE = sqrt(mean(dire_error^2))     )   }) )  round(multidimensional_comparison, 3)  #dimension MFARLR_correlation DIRE_correlation MFARLR_RMSE DIRE_RMSE #1  0.867   0.772   0.521   0.676 #2  0.816   0.724   0.588   0.724 #3  0.848   0.740   0.556   0.746 #4  0.762   0.673   0.674   0.818 #5  0.866   0.775   0.504   0.681 plot_MFARLR_MDIRE <- function(     theta,     mfarlr_first_PV,     dire_first_PV,     file = NULL ) {   theta <- as.matrix(theta)   mfarlr_first_PV <- as.matrix(mfarlr_first_PV)   dire_first_PV <- as.matrix(dire_first_PV)    stopifnot(     identical(dim(theta), dim(mfarlr_first_PV)),     identical(dim(theta), dim(dire_first_PV))   )    D <- ncol(theta)   total_panels <- D + 1L   panel_columns <- ceiling(sqrt(total_panels))   panel_rows <- ceiling(total_panels / panel_columns)    save_plot <- !is.null(file)   if (save_plot) {     grDevices::png(       filename = file,       width = 3000,       height = 2100,       res = 300     )   }    old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)   on.exit({     graphics::par(old_par)     if (save_plot && grDevices::dev.cur() > 1L) {       grDevices::dev.off()     }   }, add = TRUE)    graphics::par(     mfrow = c(panel_rows, panel_columns),     mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1),     oma = c(0, 0, 5, 0)   )    for (dimension in seq_len(D)) {     truth <- theta[, dimension]     mfarlr_pv <- mfarlr_first_PV[, dimension]     dire_pv <- dire_first_PV[, dimension]     plot_range <- range(truth, mfarlr_pv, dire_pv, finite = TRUE)      graphics::plot(       NA_real_, NA_real_,       xlim = plot_range,       ylim = plot_range,       xlab = paste0("True theta, dimension ", dimension),       ylab = "First plausible value",       main = paste0("Dimension ", dimension)     )     graphics::grid(col = "gray90")     graphics::points(       truth, dire_pv,       pch = 16, cex = 0.45,       col = grDevices::adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha.f = 0.30)     )     graphics::points(       truth, mfarlr_pv,       pch = 16, cex = 0.45,       col = grDevices::adjustcolor("darkorange", alpha.f = 0.30)     )     graphics::abline(       stats::lm(dire_pv ~ truth),       col = "steelblue", lwd = 3     )     graphics::abline(       stats::lm(mfarlr_pv ~ truth),       col = "darkorange", lwd = 3     )     graphics::abline(0, 1, col = "gray35", lwd = 2, lty = 2)   }    graphics::par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))   graphics::plot.new()   graphics::legend(     "center",     title = "Method",     legend = c("DIRE regression", "MFARLR regression", "Identity"),     col = c("steelblue", "darkorange", "gray35"),     lty = c(1, 1, 2),     lwd = c(3, 3, 2),     bty = "n",     cex = 1.05   )    unused_panels <- panel_rows * panel_columns - total_panels   if (unused_panels > 0L) {     for (panel in seq_len(unused_panels)) {       graphics::plot.new()     }   }    graphics::mtext(     "Comparison of MFARLR and DIRE Plausible Values",     side = 3,     outer = TRUE,     line = 2,     cex = 1.5,     font = 2   )    invisible(file) }  plot_MFARLR_MDIRE(   theta = sim_m1$theta,   mfarlr_first_PV = mfarlr_first_PV,   dire_first_PV = dire_first_PV,   file = "multidimensional_PV_comparison.png" )

what: FARLR Marginal Maximum Likelihood Estimation — Farlr_mml

text: Fits Factor-Adjusted Regularized Latent Regression (FARLR) model using marginal maximum likelihood (MML) framework. function serves unified interface supports multiple estimation strategies, including "FARLR_EMM" "FARLR_Debias". title: FARLR Marginal Maximum Likelihood Estimation — Farlr_mml
text: X Matrix. Covariate design matrix latent regression model, typically dimension n x p. Y Matrix. Observed item response matrix dimension n x J. parTab Data frame. Item parameter table containing least columns slope, difficulty, guessin, used define item response model. n_sam Integer. Number Monte Carlo samples per individual used approximate integrals latent traits. Defaults 5. method Character string. Estimation method used. Supported values include: "FARLR_EMM" Iterative FARLR estimation based EM–M–type   updating scheme regularization. "FARLR_Debias" FARLR estimation regularized variable   selection followed post-selection debiased refit. Defaults "FARLR_EMM". lambda Numeric vector. Candidate regularization parameters used penalized regression. Defaults seq(0.1, 0.5, = 0.1). delta.criteria Numeric. Convergence tolerance iterative updates. Defaults 1e-3. iter.max Integer. Maximum number iterations allowed value lambda. Defaults 200. window.size Integer. Window size sliding-window averaging coefficient updates used stabilize iterative estimation. Defaults 50. verbose Logical. TRUE, progress messages iteration status displayed model fitting. Defaults TRUE.

title: Simulated Dataset: 1D FARLR-Style Mixed-Format Item Responses — sim_a2
text: latent trait generated linear predictor additive noise: \(\theta = F \beta + E \nu + e\), \(e\) scaled   match target SNR. default dataset contains 15 items: eight 3PL items seven three-category GPCM items. Item slopes generated \(a_j \sim \mathrm{Lognormal}(0, 0.25)\). 3PL item, probability correct response $$P(Y_{ij}=1 \mid \theta_i) = c_j + (1-c_j)       \mathrm{logit}^{-1}\{a_j(\theta_i-b_j)\},$$ mirt intercept computed \(d_j=-a_jb_j\). GPCM item three response categories, 0, 1, 2, two step difficulties, \(b_{1j}\) \(b_{2j}\). converted mirt intercept parameterization $$d_{0j}=0,\quad d_{1j}=-a_jb_{1j},\quad       d_{2j}=-a_j(b_{1j}+b_{2j}).$$ Responses simulated using item-specific values itemtype, 3PL lower-asymptote parameters supplied guess argument mirt::simdata().
